blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Grant funding pulled them toward GHG/agriculture markets; the two-person leadership team (biz-dev + fire service, no named CTO) has nobody engineering the defense transition in parallel
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Future versions will detect a range of organic and industrial chemical gasses, including chemical warfare agents

blind_spots.blind_spot: Sensors are "compatible with several classes of small UAVs and robotic platforms" and adaptable as unattended ground sensors, yet nothing says how a threat alert reaches the operator — no TAK/ATAK integration mentioned for what is functionally a CBRN situational-awareness feed
blind_spots.operator_reality: A gas-cloud warning that is not on the squad's ATAK screen within seconds is not a warning; unattended ground sensors in a DDIL environment need a low-bandwidth tactical comms path the site never discusses
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team's sensing physics came from a national lab; the tactical data-dissemination layer is a fielding discipline outside a 3-person sensor company's experience
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our sensors can also easily be adapted to serve as unattended ground sensors for advanced warning of an approaching gas cloud

blind_spots.blind_spot: Integration story is written for commercial infrastructure ("easily integrated into existing IoT infrastructures") — the government-network reality (accreditation, RMF, controlled data from defense-lab-derived tech, possible export control) is absent
blind_spots.operator_reality: A defense-lab-derived CW sensor feeding data onto government networks needs an ATO sponsor and controlled-data handling; IoT-style onboarding does not exist on a tactical or base network
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their deployed customers so far are farms and landfills, where IoT integration genuinely is the whole story
blind_spots.evidence_quote: We are easily integrated into existing IoT infrastructures
